P23 1. A Double-Blind, Placebo-controlled Trial of
Intrathecal Baclofen Therapy in Stiff-Man
Syndrome
K. M. McEvoy, P. L. Silbert, K. A. Stolp-Smith.
J. Y. Matsumoto, P. G. McManis, and B. A. Elliott,
Rochester, MN
We undertook a double-blind placebo-controlled trial of in-
trathecal baclofen (ITB) in stiff-man syndrome (SMS). Three
patients unresponsive to current therapy (combinations of
clonazepam, baclofen, valproate, and prednisone) with a 4-,
6-, and 10-year history of SMS were studied. Current medi-
cations were continued and patients received 50 mcg of ITB
or placebo on sequential days. Patients completed a subjec-
tive evaluation, in addition to clinical and video evaluations,
and electrophysiological measures to quantify muscle activity.
Following ITB all patients demonstrated improvement in
muscle tone and electrically induced muscle activity. Ob jec-
tive (video) and subjective clinical improvement was evident
in 1 patient, who differed from the others studied by a longer
duration of disease, greater severity of stiffness, and less fear
of falling. Two patients subjectively deteriorated following
ITB, primarily due to difficulty adjusting to the reduction in
lower-limb muscle tone. Some SMS patients may be better
assessed with a short-term continuous infusion of ITB (rather
than a single dose) to allow more accurate dose titration and
for the patient to adjust to alterations in limb and axial "stiff-
ness." Potential risks of long-term ITB such as infection and
sudden baclofen withdrawal due to pump malfunction, need
to be considered.
P232. Mortality and Nursing Home Placement in
Advanced Parkinson's Disease: Follow-up of
Hallucinating Patients
ChriJtopher G. Goetz and Glenn T. Stebbins, Chicago, IL
In a prior case-control study, we found that hallucinations
were a more significant risk factor than either dementia or
motor disability for nursing home placement in patients with
advanced Parkinson's disease. This follow-up report com-
pares mortality of the original 11 cases admitted to nursing
homes and the 22 control patients originally remaining in the
community, but matched for gender, age within 2 years, and
disease duration within 2 years. As of February 1, 1994, all
original nursing home cases were dead. In contrast, 7 of 22
original control patients died in the same time period. (x2 =
11.14; p < 0.001): 4 at home and 2 within 18 months after
admission to a nursing home. Four subjects from the original
community-dwelling control group entered nursing homes
during the follow-up period. Comparison of these subjects'
last recorded Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale
(UPDRS) scores prior to nursing home placement with the
last outpatient visit in community-dwelling patients con-
firmed our original observation: Motor and intellectual im-
pairment scores were similar between the 2 groups (UPDRS
motor and intellectual function scores, Hoehn & Yahr stage,
all p > 0.05). However, the presence of hallucinations (de-
fined as a score of 2 3 on thought disorder question) was
significantly more frequent among patients transferred to
nursing homes (4 of 4 vs. 1 of 18, x2 = 11.68, p .< 0.001).
This study demonstrates a high Parkinson's disease mortality
associated with nursing home placement and reinforces the
strong relationship between hallucinations and the decision
to place patients in chronic care facilities.
P233.
Carlos Singer, Lisa M. Shulman, Augusta Parra, and
William J. Weiner, Miami, FL
Our objective was to investigate the clinical variables ef-
fecting response to botulinum toxin (BTX) injections in
spasmodic torticollis (ST) using subjective, objective, and
combined subjective/objective ratings. Thirty BTX-naive pa-
tients with idiopathic ST were treated with initial and booster
BTX injections. Clinical variables were correlated with sub-
jective ratings of discomfort, head movement, and improve-
ment; objective ratings (Toronto Western ST Severity Rating
Scale), and a combined subjective and objective rating index.
Age, duration of symptoms, objective dystonia severity, type
of head deviation, number of muscles injected, and BTX
quantity did not correlate with response. The female gender
was correlated with greater objective improvement (p =
0.046). Subjective improvement was greatest among pa-
tients with greater pretreatment subjective disability (p =
0.0000 15 and p = 0.029) or greater range of motion of the
neck (p = 0.032). The combined subjective/objective index
corroborated these findings. More pronounced subjective
disability, female gender, and greater range of motion of the
head are associated with better BTX response. Subjective
and objective rating scales reveal distinct information, and
are both important in predicting outcome following BTX
injection.

POSTER PRESENTATION:
NEUROMUSCULAR DISEASE
P234. The Mitochondrial tRNAku'UUR) Mutation at
nt-3243 Is Associated with Mitochondrial
Proliferation and Abnormal Processing in
Tissues from MELAS Patients
P. Kaufmann, Y. Koga, M. Hirano, M. P. King, S. DiMauro,
and E. A. Schon, New York, NY
MELAS, a maternally-inherited disorder characterized by mi-
tochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-
like episodes, is associated with a point mutation at mtDNA
position 3243 in the tRNALe"'UUR' gene. In order to study
further the pathogenesis of MELAS, we analyzed tissues from
8 MELAS-3243 patients, including 4 postmortem cases. The
proportion of mutant mtDNA showed little variation among
tissues in 3 out of the 4 postmortem cases. In the fourth
autopsy, the ratio of mutant: wild-type mtDNA ranged from
59% in kidney to 89% in brain, indicating that mitotic segre-
gation may occur in MELAS. Southern blot analysis of DNA
from this patient showed a significant increase in the ratio of
mitochondrial DNA: nuclear DNA in all tissues examined,
demonstrating that mitochondrial proliferation is ubiquitous,
and is not confined to ragged-red fibers in muscle. However,
the degree of mitochondrial proliferation was not correlated
to the proportion of mutant mtDNA. In Northern blot
analysis, we demonstrated the accumulation of WA 19,
a polycistronic transcript corresponding to 16s rWA,
tRNALeu(UUR), and ND1 (which are contiguous genes in the
mtDNA) in heart, kidney, and muscle. These in vivo results
are consistent with our previous in vitro studies, and support
the significance of abnormal mitochondrial RNA processing
in the pathogenesis of MELAS.
